scope: forgetting a span on the CPU reference KV backend (seeded random tiny model, raised prompt limits): the span is a revocable Derived prompt segment, forget is revoking its lineage identity and running the prompt without it (parent-chained chunk keys, no mid-sequence eviction primitive); bitwise equality of the KV state and of the next-token logits with a fresh prefill without the span, and 32 canary probes; a regression guard for forget semantics
limitations: the mechanism is lineage revocation plus parent-chained chunk keys, not a mid-sequence eviction primitive; the catalog has none

stale reuse is nearly structural to rule out (a chunk key hashes its parent chain): a pass is the expected outcome, and only the negative control (a StaleDonor probe under a suppressed index update) shows the criteria can fail
tiny seeded random model, CPU reference path, one machine profile: nothing about a trained model, a GPU kernel or a non-deterministic reduction order

the probe is the 256-entry next-token logits vector after a 16-byte suffix at one position, plus the KV-state digest of K and V rows for all prompt positions; a trace outside them (timing, memory, uncached activations) is not covered
canary_logit_shift is an integer count of f32 ulps (0 iff the maximum absolute difference is exactly 0); canaries 16 to 31 never appear in the span
model_pin_mismatches and procedure_mismatches are weak metrics (base checkpoint, topology and the canary generator seed are constants; the rest is read from the backend and the requests built)
timings come from one shared cloud container; no capacity claim
